Over the past week, rumors about Apple launching AirPods with built-in cameras have been flying everywhere. Here's a roundup of everything we've gathered this week about the camera-equipped AirPods Pro.

Latest News on Camera-Equipped AirPods Pro

It all started on Monday, when someone discovered AirPods with built-in cameras in a video from the macOS 26.7 beta. In the video, a person wearing AirPods Pro holds up a book and asks Siri to use Visual Intelligence to take note of the book.

In the video, the camera-equipped AirPods Pro look almost identical to the existing AirPods Pro 3.

Besides the video, macOS 26.7 also contains extensive code references to AirPods with built-in cameras, further revealing how they operate.

According to code seen by 9to5Mac, Apple will use a new framework called AccessorySensorMgrd to control image capture and other functions on the camera-equipped AirPods. In the code, Apple refers to this camera sensor as the "Kino Sensor."

  • Each AirPods Pro earbud has its own camera, and they operate in a paired manner, capturing simultaneously. AccessorySensorMgrd will pair the two images together. However, if only one image is captured, the framework will automatically generate a blank corresponding image.
  • The macOS 26.7 code mentions two "capture modes": active and passive. The active mode appears to capture one image from each AirPod, or provide a "capture rate" to continuously transmit images at a specified frequency.
  • The framework monitors several parameters, including image width and height, pixel binning, and left/right X/Y axis offsets, among others.
  • The framework also mentions that AirPods Pro will feature a privacy indicator light that turns on during image capture.

On the other hand, a MacRumors forum user also uncovered some details about the AirPods Pro camera resolution:

Active capture mode starts capturing at 640×640 and outputs a processed 1024×1024 image. This means the sampled image data is approximately 0.4 megapixels, while the output image is slightly over 1 megapixel. There's also another lower-resolution passive capture mode that captures at 320×320 and can output 320×320 or 512×512 images depending on the capture mode. These are specific capture resolutions; the physical sensor's native resolution may be larger.

The forum member also provided more details about "passive mode," which is described as "lower resolution and supports environmental awareness." macOS 26 lists five possible triggers for passive capture:

  • Ambient sound
  • Audio scene changes
  • Posture changes
  • Head movement
  • "Circular area, meaning the user has left the preset spatial range."

Launch Date for Camera-Equipped AirPods

Naturally, the appearance of this video and related code references in the macOS 26.7 beta immediately sparked intense speculation that the product could arrive any time, potentially debuting as early as next month alongside the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Ultra at Apple's event.

However, according to a Bloomberg report, that is not the case. Mark Gurman noted in a Wednesday report that the camera-equipped AirPods remain on track for a 2027 launch.

Gurman explained that Apple is internally developing two versions of this product:

  • B790: The version seen in the video. Essentially an improved version of AirPods Pro 3, but with cameras added.
  • B798: A brand new generation of AirPods (such as AirPods Pro 4), also with cameras added.

It remains unclear which version Apple will ultimately choose to release, but either way, the earliest we can expect to see it is next year.

Bloomberg's report also reiterated that the AirPods Pro cameras will not be used for taking photos or videos. Instead, they are designed to "scan the surrounding environment and provide contextual information for the Siri digital assistant and other AI tools."

Summary

In summary, this week has indeed released a substantial amount of new information about camera-equipped AirPods, including details on features and how they operate.

What do you think about Apple adding cameras to AirPods Pro? Do you think it's a good idea? Feel free to share your thoughts with us in the comments section.
